media.alt: One-third of the world's population infected with TB

content.text: World tuberculosis Day is being observed this year with the knowledge that every third person in the world is infected with TB. This year, the Day will focus on the efforts of frontline TB care providers and their crucial role in stopping TB. The section of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine, Aga Khan University held a seminar on Tuesday which covered different aspects of the fight against TB especially in the context that 33 % of TB cases in the world occur in the South-East Asia Region.

Experts at the seminar pointed out that incomplete or poorly supervised treatment regimens cause the bacilli to develop resistance to drugs and people infected later carry the same resistant strain. They said that incomplete or poor treatment was worse than no treatment at all.

Dr Ahmed Suleman Haque, Dr Rumina Hassan, Dr Mohammad Wassay, Dr Muhammad Irfan, Dr Ali bin Sarwar Zuberi, Dr Nisar Ahmed Rao of Aga Khan University addressed the seminar while Professor Nadeem Rizvi, head of Department of Chest Diseases, JPMC Karachi delivered the keynote address.

It is estimated that 1.75 million deaths resulted from TB in 2003 while one new person is infected with TB bacilli every second in the world. World TB Day aims to mobilise support for fighting the spread of TB prominently on global agenda and ensure its elimination by 2050.

Held annually on 24 March, the Day commemorates the date in 1882 when Dr Robert Koch presented his discovery of the TB bacillus to a group of doctors in Berlin. The United Nations Millennium Development Goals include cutting down TB prevalence and death rates to half of the present rate by 2015.
